items.title: Counting backwards: The prior-price rule and the regulation of discount claims in Indian e-commerce
items.summary: A discount is a comparison and a comparison is only as reliable as its reference point. A struck-through figure beside a lower price represents that the lower price is a genuine concession. Indian law has so far policed that representation only after the event, through the general prohibition on misleading advertisements. The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026 , notified on September 9, 2026 and in force from January 1, 2027, add a direct rule. Rule 4(13) requires an e-commerce entity or seller that announces a price reduction to disclose a “prior price” alongside the reduced price. This article argues that Rule 4(13) rests on a sound benchmark but leaves four questions open: what period the benchmark covers, how prominently it must be shown, who bears the duty on a marketplace and how a claim can be tested. Chugh succeeds Shobhana Nikam, who has decided to step down for personal reasons, effective October 31, 2026, following a four-year tenure. Bengaluru-based Chugh will report directly to Praveen Someshwar, CEO & President, India with a dotted line reporting to Global General Counsel Randall Ingber. He will also join the India Executive Committee and the Global Legal Leadership Team. items.title: Theni jailbreak: Last 4 of escaped prisoners caught
items.summary: The last four of the 17 remand prisoners who escaped from the District Jail at Thekkampatti in Tamil Nadu's Theni district were taken into custody on Wednesday, October 28, with the last two accused surrendering. The latest two, identified as siblings Thirupathi and Meenatchi Sundaram, surrendered at the Kudalur police station while two other accused, Regin and Ponmuthuselvam, were arrested earlier in the day. The jailbreak took place late on Monday, October 26, when the prisoners allegedly attacked prison staff and fled the premises. According to the Prison Department, the incident occurred around 10 pm when some inmates raised an alarm, claiming that a prisoner in the third block was experiencing an epileptic seizure. When Grade II warden Stalin Prabhu, who was on duty in the block, entered to check on the prisoner, the inmates who were lodged in the same cell allegedly attacked him and attempted to escape. They then allegedly confronted guards, snatched the keys, and opened the main entrance to flee the prison.
